title: Mercury Systems — marketplace & channel integration intro
header: Date: 2026-07-18 | Start: 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~62m | Recording: enabled
summary: Introductory discovery between Redwood AE/SE and Mercury partnerships + platform team to explore a marketplace/channel integration for GPU-hosted workloads. Covered business objectives, technical constraints (VPC, KMS, SOC2), rough timeline, and next steps for a pilot + pricing/packaging discussion.
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. I'm Alex from Redwood, AE on the partner program. Priya from our solutions team is with me. 
[00:09] Ben Thornton: Hi Alex, hey Priya, thanks — Ben here. We wanted to understand how Redwood could fit into Mercury's marketplace offering, right — we have customers asking for managed GPU inference endpoints.
[00:21] Priya Shah: Yep, great. Quick agenda: we want to hear Mercury's goals, existing infra, key constraints, then sketch integration patterns (hosted, dedicated, private), and flag any security items.
[00:33] Marta Ruiz: Sounds good — quick context, Mercury runs a channel marketplace that bundles compute from partner providers, we surface it to our enterprise buyers, and lately there's demand for LLM inference as a managed option.
[00:44] Liang Wu: Technical point — our infra is AWS-first, accounts per customer, we do VPC peering for managed services, and we already have a KMS/HSM strategy for keys.
[00:55] Alex Martinez: Cool. So customers want a turnkey inference offering — important question: is Mercury expecting Redwood to run the model instances on Mercury-owned GPU nodes, or do you want Redwood-hosted endpoints that are discoverable in the marketplace?
[01:12] Ben Thornton: Ideally both over time. MVP: Redwood-hosted endpoints that appear as a marketplace SKU. Longer term, if partners want private deployments we could support an on-prem or partner-hosted variant.
[01:27] Priya Shah: Okay that's a common pattern. For Redwood-hosted marketplace SKUs we can publish model variants with pricing and SLO. For partner-hosted we have Redwood Private options — though there are more network and onboarding steps.
[01:41] Liang Wu: Can you explain the differences in latency and cost between Redwood Dedicated vs hosted variants? We've got customers worried about tail latency for chat-like flows.
[01:52] Priya Shah: Sure — Dedicated gives predictable latency and capacity because it's reserved GPU pools. Hosted (our shared catalog) is lower friction but can see more variance; we do routing/fallbacks and auto-burst but it isn't the same isolation. We also have batching, KV cache, and quantization recommendations to reduce token cost.
[02:12] Ben Thornton: What's the typical integration for marketplace listing — is there an API or is it a packaging + validation step?
[02:19] Alex Martinez: We can do both. For quick listing we provide a marketplace-ready manifest and a short validation checklist. For deeper integrations you can call our APIs for provisioning, billing links, and telemetry embed so Mercury can display usage. We'll share a sample manifest after the call. (link: drive.redwood/mercury/manifest.pdf)
[02:39] Speaker 1: Sorry — quick interjection, do you support SSO for our customers to access the console?
[02:45] Priya Shah: Yes, we support SAML SSO, SCIM for user sync, RBAC. For partner flows we can also exchange tokens so your portal can embed endpoints without separate user flows.
[02:57] Marta Ruiz: On compliance, enterprises ask for SOC 2 and ISO reports. Do you provide those?
[03:03] Alex Martinez: We have SOC 2 Type II reports and ISO certs for the Redwood hosted API. For private deployments, compliance boundaries are different — we provide audit log hooks and you can bring your own KMS/HSM.
[03:16] Liang Wu: About KMS — we want customer keys to remain in customer KMS, is that possible for a partner-hosted variant?
[03:23] Priya Shah: Yes — for Redwood Private we integrate with customer-managed KMS and HSM. For hosted SKUs we offer envelope encryption and you're welcome to use your own KMS for key material where the partner flow allows.
[03:34] Ben Thornton: Timeline question — if Mercury wants to onboard two marketplace SKUs as a pilot in Q4, what's realistic from Redwood's side?
[03:42] Alex Martinez: If we do hosted endpoints it can be a few weeks for manifest + listing + basic validation. If you want co-branded telemetry and billing integration plus pilot SLAs, maybe 6–8 weeks to be safe. Partner-hosted or private on-prem would be 8–12+ depending on network certs and keys.
[03:58] Marta Ruiz: For the pilot success criteria: our buyer needs <200ms p95 for simple completion endpoints and predictable unit cost under $0.02/token equivalent. Are those achievable?
[04:09] Priya Shah: p95 under 200ms depends on model size and sequence length. For small to medium models we can tune kernels, batching, and prefer dedicated pools for strict p95. Cost target will depend on model and quantization; we can model that once you pick target model family.
[04:28] Liang Wu: Do you have a way to stress-test routing and provisioning? We'd like to see warmup and scale behavior.
[04:34] Priya Shah: Yes, we can run a perf estimate and a small benchmark against a synthetic workload. We'll propose a perf script and expected token throughput per GPU during the pilot.
[04:43] Ben Thornton: Any red flags you see from what we said?
[04:46] Alex Martinez: The key bits are network topology for partner-hosted, KMS agreements, and agreeing on an SLA for the marketplace listing. Also commercial alignment on revenue share / billing flow.
[04:59] Marta Ruiz: On billing, Mercury prefers a gross-to-net model where we bill customers and remit a share to the vendor. Is that supported?
[05:06] Alex Martinez: We support multiple billing flows. For marketplace we can do passthrough invoicing or partner settlement. We'll map options in the partner agreement.
[05:16] Liang Wu: Technical deep dive — how does Redwood handle KV cache and prefix caching? We want clarity on stateful session reuse across calls when the gateway is multi-tenant.
[05:26] Priya Shah: Good question — we have automatic prefix and KV cache strategies. For multi-tenant marketplace SKUs we isolate KV cache per customer/session token, and for dedicated pools we optimize in-memory KV layers for lower latency. There are config knobs for cache TTL and warmup.
[05:42] Speaker 2: There's some background noise, sorry.
[05:45] Alex Martinez: No worries. Quick ask — can you share a rough list of customer profiles and anticipated QPS across your top 3 buyers? That will help us size the pilot.
[05:56] Ben Thornton: I can share anonymized numbers — I'll send a short spreadsheet after the call.
[06:01] Marta Ruiz: Also we need partner program docs — lead routing, referral credits, co-marketing tiers.
[06:08] Alex Martinez: We'll share our partner deck and a short PRD for the marketplace SKU. (link: /s/mercury/redwood-partner-deck.pdf)
[06:17] Priya Shah: Tech ask: if you want to run a partner-hosted variant on Mercury-owned GPUs, we need a small installer and a config checklist — basically network, ports, and KMS endpoint details. We also have an operator for Kubernetes deployments if partners prefer K8s.
[06:35] Liang Wu: We mostly run K8s on EKS. The operator approach sounds easier. Any cert requirements?
[06:41] Priya Shah: TLS mutual auth, cert pinning for control-plane connections, and you may want to open specific egress ranges. We'll provide an infra checklist.
[06:50] Ben Thornton: Competitive landscape — our procurement asked if Redwood can integrate better than competitors like ApexCloud and NebulaCompute. How do you typically differentiate?
[06:59] Alex Martinez: We lean on production-grade runtime, unified interface across hosted/dedicated/private, and our pricing/config tooling (Optimize) that suggests quantization and batching tradeoffs. We'll share benchmark links and a short comparison doc.
[07:13] Marta Ruiz: Are there any proprietary model restrictions we should be aware of for marketplace SKUs?
[07:18] Priya Shah: We curate open models and also support customer-provided model binaries in private deployments. For hosted public SKUs we surface verified models; for partner-hosted you can run customer models subject to license compliance.
[07:31] Alex Martinez: Ok let's recap next steps and owners.
[07:34] Priya Shah: I'll run a perf estimate + sample perf script for the pilot.
[07:38] Ben Thornton: We'll send anonymized QPS and a list of candidate buyers.
[07:41] Alex Martinez: We'll send partner deck, manifest sample, and partner agreement options.
[07:45] Marta Ruiz: We'll confirm internal stakeholders and timeline — target Q4 pilot.
[07:50] Liang Wu: I'll review the operator prerequisites and will try a quick lab install once we get the checklist.
[07:56] Alex Martinez: Great, thanks all. We'll follow up with the doc bundle and proposed dates for a technical onboarding session.
[08:03] Ben Thornton: Thanks everyone, talk soon.
[08:07] [call ends]
